newsitem.title: UK: First rain in south-east Britain since March 4.
newsitem.headline: First rain in south-east Britain since March 4.

text.p: London and south-eastern Britain enjoyed the first significant rainfall since March 4 on Friday and Saturday, bringing more than 8 mm of rain over the two days, the London Weather Centre said.

Steady rain also fell over much of the rest of the country but looked likely to die out on Sunday and the forecast for the rest of the week was occasional showers giving way to a return to largely fine weather, a spokesman said.

A dry spell in much of northwest Europe has helped drive world wheat prices to 1997 highs around $4.25 per bushel in Chicago futures. The European Union imposed a tax on Thursday to curb wheat exports and thereby keep a lid on internal prices.
The London Weather Centre spokesman said the rainfall was unlikely to have made a significant difference to the drought in much of the nation.
First reports said most of Friday and Saturday's rain had simply disappeared through huge dry cracks in farming land.
In France, light rains brought relief on Saturday to farmers in many parts of the country suffering from a prolonged dry spell, Meteo France said.
More light rain was forecast in many areas for Sunday in the third wave of wet weather sweeping in from the Atlantic since Friday. "The amounts are not huge," a forecaster said.
